skill.name: oss-hunter
skill.description: Find promising open source contribution opportunities by researching active GitHub repositories and labeled issues.
skill.summary: Helps agents build concise dossiers for open source issues worth investigating.

content.value_statement: Finding useful open source issues can take hours of manual searching. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to research active repositories and prepare contribution dossiers.
actual_capabilities: Searches for active GitHub repositories using web search or GitHub CLI workflows.
Prioritizes repositories with strong stars, recent activity, and relevant technical topics.
Looks for issue labels such as help-wanted, good-first-issue, bug, and roadmap.
Evaluates issue impact, reproducibility, mergeability, and estimated complexity.
Produces a concise contribution dossier with project, issue, strategy, and confidence details.
limitations: Requires web search access or an available gh CLI for best results.
Does not guarantee that maintainers will accept a pull request.
Large repositories may exceed the agent context window during deeper review.
Repository activity and issue labels can become outdated quickly.

use_cases.title: Plan a First Contribution
use_cases.description: Find beginner-friendly issues in active projects and understand why each issue is worth considering.

use_cases.title: Build a Contribution Pipeline
use_cases.description: Identify several promising repositories and compare their issue quality, maintainer activity, and expected effort.

use_cases.title: Target High-Impact Fixes
use_cases.description: Research bug reports in popular repositories and outline practical fix strategies before starting implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Find Beginner Issues
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search across a topic area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find good first issues in active Python open source projects. Give me three options with links and a short reason for each.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Help Wanted Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Hunt for help wanted issues in AI tooling repositories. Rank them by impact, mergeability, and estimated effort.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Contribution Dossier
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed planning for a selected repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a contribution dossier for open issues in owner/repo. Include root cause notes, likely files to inspect, and a fix strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Strategic Contributions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced portfolio planning across multiple projects.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find high-impact OSS issues in developer infrastructure projects. Prioritize issues that could become strong portfolio work and explain the tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Find help wanted issues in active AI repositories.
output_examples.output: A ranked shortlist of repositories, issue links, labels, estimated effort, maintainer activity notes, and a recommended first target.

output_examples.input: Generate a dossier for a bug in a selected repository.
output_examples.output: A concise dossier with issue summary, suspected root cause, investigation steps, proposed fix, risk notes, and confidence score.

output_examples.input: Compare two open source issues for contribution value.
output_examples.output: A comparison of user impact, implementation difficulty, review likelihood, and which issue is better to start first.

best_practices: Provide a topic, language, or repository scope before starting a hunt.
Ask for links, labels, maintainer activity, and confidence scores in every dossier.
Verify the selected issue manually before writing code or opening a pull request.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a labeled issue is easy without reading the discussion.
Do not target inactive repositories without checking recent maintainer responses.
Do not submit automated fixes before confirming project contribution guidelines.

faq.question: What does this skill help me find?
faq.answer: It helps find open source issues that may be practical, impactful, and suitable for a contribution.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: No, but GitHub CLI improves structured searches when it is installed and authenticated.

faq.question: Can it guarantee pull request acceptance?
faq.answer: No. Maintainers decide what they accept, and project needs can change at any time.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should I provide in my prompt?
faq.answer: Provide a topic, language, repository, or experience level so the search can stay focused.

faq.question: Does it write code for the issue?
faq.answer: It focuses on discovery and planning. You can ask your agent to continue into implementation after review.
